rows.title: Monetary Policy
rows.figure: Fed Dec quarter-point hike ~96% (CME FedWatch, Nov 25 close, via Hercules); ECB Dec ~93%; BoJ Dec ~85%; BoC Dec ~80%, all six big Canadian banks forecast a hike; BoE Dec ~80–82%; RBA Dec hold ~99%; de Cos backed as ECB president from Feb 2027
rows.read: A December Fed hike stays all but certain, and the European Central Bank's October notes confirm a December rise there too. Euro-area leaders picked a centrist to lead the European Central Bank from February, and every big Canadian bank now expects a Bank of Canada hike.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: Beige Book: growth in 8 of 12 Fed regions, none declined; Australia Q3 private capex +12.2% q/q (fcst 4.5%); Germany GfK Dec −30.2 (fcst −29.4)
rows.read: Australian firms stepped up investment far more than expected, and the Fed's Beige Book found most US regions still growing. German consumers stayed deeply gloomy. Strong growth backs higher rates in the US and Australia, while Europe lags.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: US core PCE Oct +3.3% y/y (fcst 3.2%); Australia CPI Oct 4.9% y/y; Tokyo core CPI Nov due 5:30 PM CT Thu (fcst 3.0%, Oct 2.6%)
rows.read: US core inflation edged up again in October, and Australian inflation is climbing. In Japan, a rate-setter said a weak yen and costly raw materials are pushing prices up, ahead of Tokyo's November figures tonight. All three keep their central banks leaning against easing.

rows.title: Risk Sentiment
rows.figure: Two Italian workers killed in Kuwait drone attack; Jazan refinery hit, one killed; EUR/CHF ~0.9152 (+0.36%); AUD/USD ~0.6635; US markets closed for Thanksgiving
rows.read: The Gulf fighting spread, with deadly attacks in Kuwait and on a Saudi refinery, but markets looked past it in thin holiday trade. European shares rose and the franc lost ground against the euro. The Bank of England warned that borrowing to fund artificial intelligence is a growing risk to the financial system.

rows.figure: Brent ~$94–96 in thin trade, no Thanksgiving settlement (Hercules ~$93.83 at 2:37 PM CT; FinanceFeeds $95.58 midday London); Wed settle $94.61; WTI ~$84.63; gold ~$3,567, Wed low ~$3,446
rows.read: Oil held near $95 as attacks around the Gulf kept supply fears alive, though no barrels were lost. That helps the Canadian dollar and costs Japan and the euro area. Gold steadied after bouncing from its lowest in more than a year.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: Hedge funds (CFTC, Nov 17): USD index −1.3K (flipped short), EUR −76.6K, GBP +28.8K, JPY −23.8K, CHF −19.8K, CAD −72.1K, AUD +38.0K, NZD −23.6K; asset managers GBP −104.6K, AUD −182.7K, EUR +147.2K
rows.read: The latest weekly figures show hedge funds have turned slightly against the dollar, while still betting against the euro, the kiwi, the franc and, most strongly, the Canadian dollar. They still bet on the pound and the Aussie, where big long-term investors take the opposite side. Heavy bets against the loonie leave room for a fast unwind if Canadian hike bets keep growing.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: USTR proposed Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies: up to 15% EU, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, Switzerland; up to 20% extra China; 25% India; 35% Vietnam; comments due Jan 5, hearings Jan 25 (USTR); S&P France review Fri Nov 27
rows.read: The US plans new tariffs on 14 economies, but nothing takes effect before early 2027. France's debts remain a weight on the euro, with S&P due to review its credit rating on Friday, November 27.
